data.name: メモリーズオフ2nd
data.detailed_description:
*This game is only available in Japanese, Traditional Chinese, and Simplified Chinese.

「メモリーズオフ」シリーズ２作目
2001年に登場した恋愛アドベンチャーゲーム「メモリーズオフ2nd」をフルＨＤ移植。

ストーリーを読み進め、選択肢を選んでいくシンプルなアドベンチャーゲーム方式を採用。
選択肢でストーリーが分岐。複数のエンディングへと進んでいきます。

収録シナリオ
本編
雪螢
AfterStory


Introduction
かけがえのない想いと引き換えに……

主人公「伊波健」は、私立の高校に通う高校３年生。
ずっと変わらないと、信じていた。
半年前から交際している同級生の「白河ほたる」との幸せな状況も、２人の関係も。

しかし、ある出来事を境に変化が訪れる。
些細な誤解。すれ違う心……。
小さな変化は、やがて取り返しのつかないところまで膨らんで……。

そんな最中、２人の間にある数え切れぬほどの想い出を振り切ってでも、一緒にいたいと思える女性が現れたとしたら……。

健は選ぶことができるのだろうか？
これから共に、かけがえのない想い出を築いていく、その人を────。


STAFF
キャラクターデザイン：ささきむつみ
シナリオ：打越鋼太郎、中澤工、日暮茶坊、三浦洋晃、西川眞音、館山緑、笹成稀多郎



キャスト：
白河ほたる：水樹奈々
南つばめ：池澤春菜
飛世巴：仲西環
寿々奈鷹乃：千葉紗子
白河静流：菊池志穂
相摩希・望：南里侑香

舞方香菜：松来未祐
稲穂信：間島淳司
中森翔太：福山潤
霧島小夜子：浅野るり

reviews.review:
Memories Off 2nd is a character-driven romantic visual novel that places emotional uncertainty at the center of its story rather than treating romance as a simple pursuit with an inevitable happy conclusion. Developed by MAGES. Inc. and published by Spike Chunsoft Co., Ltd., this Full HD adaptation preserves the identity of the classic second installment while making its artwork and presentation more comfortable on modern displays. Its age is still noticeable in its artistic conventions and straightforward interface, but those qualities also give it a distinctive early visual novel atmosphere that separates it from more contemporary releases.

The story follows Ken Inami, a third-year high school student who has been dating his classmate Hotaru Shirakawa for around six months. Ken believes their relationship is stable and that the happiness they share will continue. That confidence begins to disappear after an incident creates misunderstandings between them. Small disagreements and emotional distance gradually develop into something more serious, forcing Ken to reconsider feelings that once appeared certain. This is where the narrative becomes particularly effective, because the conflict does not depend entirely on dramatic external events. Much of the tension comes from ordinary relationship problems such as poor communication, jealousy, hesitation, conflicting expectations, and the inability to say what someone genuinely feels.

The introduction of other women complicates Ken's situation further. Instead of beginning the story as an unattached protagonist choosing between several potential partners, he already has a meaningful relationship and a collection of memories with Hotaru. Pursuing another person therefore carries emotional consequences. The game repeatedly explores whether past happiness is enough reason to preserve a relationship and whether memories should determine someone's future. It gives romantic choices a bittersweet quality because choosing one direction can mean abandoning another person and accepting that something once considered permanent has changed.

Gameplay follows a traditional visual novel structure. Most of the experience consists of reading conversations and narration before making decisions at important moments. Those choices determine how relationships develop and eventually lead into different routes and endings. There are no elaborate gameplay mechanics competing for attention, making this primarily an experience for players who enjoy lengthy dialogue, character development, and branching storytelling. Some decisions may initially appear insignificant, but their cumulative effect can substantially change the direction of Ken's relationships. This encourages multiple playthroughs, particularly for anyone interested in understanding every major character rather than stopping after a single ending.

The package contains more than the central storyline, incorporating the main scenario together with Yuki Hotaru, AfterStory, and Introduction content. These additional scenarios strengthen the overall package and provide more material for players invested in the characters. Multiple endings also give completionists a reason to explore alternative decisions. The 13 Steam achievements provide another modest incentive to experience more of the available routes, although the narrative consequences of different choices remain a much stronger reason to replay the game than achievement hunting.

Its character presentation is one of the game's strongest qualities. The cast includes Hotaru Shirakawa, Tsubame Minami, Tomoe Tobise, Takano Suzuna, Shizuru Shirakawa, Nozomi and Megumi Soma, Kana Maikata, Shin Inaho, Shota Nakamori, and Sayoko Kirishima. Rather than existing solely as alternative romantic targets or supporting faces, these characters help broaden the emotional circumstances surrounding Ken. The Japanese voice performances are especially valuable, adding personality to conversations that can range from relaxed everyday interactions to uncomfortable and emotionally charged confrontations. Nana Mizuki's role as Hotaru is particularly important because the effectiveness of the central relationship depends heavily on making her feel like a person with genuine emotional investment rather than simply an obstacle standing between the protagonist and alternative routes.

Visually, the Full HD treatment improves clarity without erasing the game's historical identity. Mutsumi Sasaki's character designs retain the recognizable aesthetic of Japanese visual novels from their era. Players accustomed to modern character artwork may find the style dated initially, but it possesses warmth and personality. The presentation ultimately complements the nostalgic tone of the experience. This is closer to a carefully preserved classic than a complete visual remake, so anyone approaching it should expect traditional backgrounds, character portraits, dialogue boxes, and largely static storytelling rather than extensive animation.

The most important limitation is language support. English is not supported, while Japanese, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese are available for interface text and subtitles, with Japanese providing full audio. Because reading is essentially the entire gameplay experience, this is not a minor inconvenience. Players unable to comfortably understand one of the supported written languages will struggle to experience the narrative as intended.

Steam Deck compatibility is excellent. Memories Off 2nd is Steam Deck Verified. Its functionality is accessible with the default controller configuration, appropriate Steam Deck controller icons are displayed, interface text is considered readable on the handheld screen, and the default graphics configuration performs properly. It also runs successfully under SteamOS. A dialogue-heavy visual novel is naturally well suited to handheld sessions, making the Deck one of the more comfortable ways to experience the game.

Memories Off 2nd ultimately succeeds through emotional storytelling rather than mechanical complexity. Its exploration of relationships becoming fragile through misunderstandings, changing feelings, and difficult choices remains compelling despite the game's age. The branching structure rewards players willing to examine the characters from several perspectives, while the additional scenarios make this Full HD edition a substantial presentation of the second Memories Off story. Its lack of English localization significantly limits accessibility, but for players who can read one of its supported languages, this remains a thoughtful, bittersweet romance about choosing between treasured memories and an uncertain future.

Rating: 8/10
